title: Linux release leg builds on floating `ubuntu-latest`, so the AppImage/.deb require glibc >= 2.38 and cannot start on Ubuntu 22.04 / Debian 12 / RHEL 9 despite 'runs on most distributions'
evidence:
release.yml:105-108
          - os: ubuntu-latest
            rust_target: x86_64-unknown-linux-gnu
            recipe: build-linux-updater
            artifact: linux

objdump -T on a workspace binary built on this Ubuntu 24.04 (glibc 2.39) box:
0000000000000000      DF *UND*	0000000000000000 (GLIBC_2.38) __isoc23_sscanf
0000000000000000      DF *UND*	0000000000000000 (GLIBC_2.38) __isoc23_strtol
0000000000000000  w   DF *UND*	0000000000000000 (GLIBC_2.39) pidfd_spawnp

README.md:225-229
- **`azapptoolkit_<version>_amd64.AppImage`** — portable, runs on most
  distributions; `chmod +x` it and run.
- **`azapptoolkit_<version>_amd64.deb`** — for Debian/Ubuntu and
  derivatives

release.yml:301 (release body)
            (Row "artifacts/bundle-linux/appimage/*.AppImage" "Portable, runs on most distros (**auto-updates**); ``chmod +x`` then run."),
rationale: glibc symbol versioning binds each import to the default version of the *build* host's libc, and glibc 2.38 redirected `strtol`/`sscanf` to `__isoc23_*` under `_GNU_SOURCE`. The objdump above shows those as strong (non-weak) imports in a binary from this very workspace built on 2.39; the desktop binary additionally compiles aws-lc-sys C code, so its floor is at least the same. `ubuntu-latest` is 24.04 today (glibc 2.39) and will float again to 26.04, so the artifact's minimum distro silently changes with GitHub's runner image. Ubuntu 22.04 LTS (2.35, supported to 2027), Debian 12 (2.36) and RHEL 9 (2.34) all fail at load with "version `GLIBC_2.38' not found" — the .deb even installs cleanly first. The README/release body promise the opposite, and nothing in release.yml checks the floor. Tauri's own guidance is to build Linux bundles on the oldest distro you intend to support. Note the AppImage bundling WebKitGTK does not help; glibc is never bundled.
proposal: Pin the Linux matrix leg to `ubuntu-22.04` (or the oldest distro the README promises), and add a post-build guard step in the same job: `objdump -T target/x86_64-unknown-linux-gnu/release/azapptoolkit | grep -oE 'GLIBC_[0-9.]+' | sort -Vu | tail -1` asserted <= 2.35 so a runner-image drift fails the release instead of shipping. Document the actual floor ("needs glibc 2.35+, i.e. Ubuntu 22.04 / Debian 12 or newer") in README Linux install and the release-body Row text, and note that the runner pin is load-bearing in release-updater-demo.md. Consider the same pin for the ci.yml Linux jobs only if they produce shipped bytes (they do not today).
verifier_notes: Evidence checks out. release.yml:105-108 uses floating `ubuntu-latest` for the Linux leg; docs/architecture/release-updater-demo.md:13 just restates `ubuntu-latest`, and no doc, CHANGELOG or workflow mentions glibc or a distro floor. Reproduced the objdump on this Ubuntu 24.04 / glibc 2.39 box: target/debug/deps/azapptoolkit_auth-* imports strong `(GLIBC_2.38) __isoc23_sscanf` / `__isoc23_strtol` (the core-only binary tops out at 2.34 strong, so the 2.38 floor comes from the C deps — aws-lc-sys 0.45.0 via rustls/reqwest, and src-tauri/Cargo.toml:63 links aws-lc-rs directly, so the shipped desktop binary carries at least the same floor). README.md:225-229 and release.yml:312 promise 'runs on most distributions'; the Tauri .deb declares unversioned depends so it installs and then fails at exec on Ubuntu 22.04 (2.35) / Debian 12 (2.36) / RHEL 9 (2.34). Caveats the verdict should carry: (a) the release binary itself was not inspected here — the floor is inferred from a workspace test binary with the same C deps, which is a safe inference but not an observation; (b) jammy does ship `libwebkit2gtk-4.1-dev`, so the `ubuntu-22.04` pin is feasible, but GitHub-hosted 22.04 images have a finite life (standard support ends 2027), so the proposed objdump guard step is the load-bearing, durable part and should fail the job rather than warn. Tauri's own v2 CI guidance builds Linux on `ubuntu-22.04`. Severity high is honest for a shipped .deb/AppImage that cannot start on current LTS distros the README targets.

title: MSI and .deb installs are offered the NSIS/AppImage payload: no install-format gate in check_for_update although bundle_type() is available
rationale: The plugin resolves the download key as `{os}-{arch}-{bundle}` then `{os}-{arch}`; latest.json only carries the bare keys, so an MSI or .deb install gets `Some(update)` and the shell toasts "Update available" on every launch. On an MSI install, clicking "Update & restart" downloads the NSIS setup.exe, `extract_exe` classifies it as Nsis and `ShellExecuteW(setup.exe /P /UPDATE /R)` installs a second, per-user copy beside the per-machine MSI — exactly the outcome README:255-258 tells MSI users to avoid, and the only documented guard is the opt-out that F036/F139 found is never read. On a .deb install, `bundle_type()` is Deb so `install_deb` runs on AppImage bytes, fails `is_deb` after the full download and the raw plugin string "invalid updater binary format" lands in the splash's warn Callout (update_splash.rs:40-43). The manual "Check for updates" menu item (shell.rs:196-208) has the same blind spot. Tauri exposes the install format at runtime — `tauri::utils::platform::bundle_type()` (tauri re-exports `tauri_utils as utils`, lib.rs:115; the bundler binary-patches the `__TAURI_BUNDLE_TYPE` marker) — and the plugin already relies on it. Complements, does not duplicate, F036/F139.
proposal: In `check_for_update` (and `perform_update`), read `tauri::utils::platform::bundle_type()` and short-circuit for `Some(BundleType::Msi | BundleType::Deb | BundleType::Rpm)`. Preferably make the DTO a tri-state (`UpToDate` / `Available(UpdateInfo)` / `ManagedExternally { format }`) so the manual check can say "This MSI/.deb install is updated by your packaging tooling" instead of "You're on the latest version", and the launch check stays silent. Pull the decision into a pure `fn updatable_format(BundleType) -> bool` with a unit test, mock the new shape in the GUI shell test. Alternative worth weighing: publish `windows-x86_64-msi` and `linux-x86_64-deb` keys in latest.json (the plugin can run msiexec /passive and dpkg via pkexec) and drop the "not auto-updated" policy — but that is a policy change; the gate is the safe default.
verifier_notes: All quoted evidence is real. apps/desktop/src-tauri/src/commands/updater.rs:26-37 and :44-49 call `updater.check()` with no install-format gate. Vendored tauri-plugin-updater 2.12.0 src/updater.rs:581-582 computes `installer_for_bundle_type(bundle_type())` and `get_urls` (:608-635) falls back from `{os}-{arch}-{installer}` to the bare `{os}-{arch}` key; release.yml:213-215 publishes only bare keys, so an MSI or .deb install always gets `Some(update)`. Linux `install_inner` (:1045-1049) dispatches on `bundle_type()` and `install_deb` (:1126-1131) rejects AppImage bytes with `InvalidUpdaterFormat` only after the full download; Windows `extract_exe` (:994-1003) classifies by bytes so NSIS bytes run `setup.exe /P /UPDATE` via ShellExecuteW (:841-880) on top of a per-machine MSI. `tauri_utils::platform::bundle_type()` exists at tauri-utils-2.9.3/src/platform.rs:353-368 and is reachable as `tauri::utils::platform::bundle_type` (tauri-2.11.6/src/lib.rs:115). The only documented mitigation (README.md:196-198, :255-259, archived CHANGELOG line 3286) is the `auto_update` opt-out, and `UserSettings::load` / `.auto_update` have zero callers outside crates/azapptoolkit-core/src/settings.rs, so the README's 'disable auto-update on MSI installs' advice is inert. Not a documented deliberate decision: README/release body/CHANGELOG state the *policy* that MSI/.deb are not auto-updated, but nothing enforces it. update_splash.rs:40-43 does surface the raw plugin message. The GUI shell test (web-rs/tests/gui/shell.rs:21-24) deliberately leaves `check_for_update` unmocked, so mocking a tri-state DTO is feasible. Severity: high is defensible because the toast actively invites the wrong install on every launch with no warning, though the harm still needs two clicks (toast -> 'Update & restart'); medium-high would also be honest. Proposal is sound; the gate must only fire on `Some(Msi|Deb|Rpm)` since `bundle_type()` is `None` for dev/unbundled binaries.

title: macOS: unsigned .app + legacy-keychain default ACL means every auto-update triggers a keychain prompt (or a silent 'no session') — README says it 'updates in place like the Windows NSIS build'
evidence:

After that it launches normally and **updates in place** like the Windows
NSIS build. Apple Silicon (M-series) only for now; Intel builds aren't
published yet.

token_cache.rs:55-57 (legacy keychain store, default ACL)
        let store =
            apple_native_keyring_store::keychain::Store::new().map_err(|e| e.to_string())?;

vendored apple-native-keyring-store/src/keychain.rs:72-74
        self.get_keychain()?
            .set_generic_password(&self.service, &self.account, secret)

DEVELOPMENT.md:161-164
The builds are **unsigned / not notarized**, so first launch hits
Gatekeeper — ...  (Apple notarization
can be layered on later by adding the Developer-ID secrets + `APPLE_*` env

commands/auth.rs:39-43 (a keyring error at launch is swallowed)
        Err(err) => {
            let code = UiError::from(err).code;
            tracing::info!(target: "auth", %code, "no session to restore; showing sign-in");
            Ok(None)
rationale: Legacy-keychain items created with `SecKeychainAddGenericPassword` get an ACL naming the creating application. For code without a Developer-ID signature there is no stable designated requirement — the trusted-app entry is bound to the specific binary — so after the updater swaps `/Applications/azapptoolkit.app` (plugin `install_inner`, rename of the bundle) the new binary is a different app to Keychain Services. The next `find_generic_password` in `restore_session` raises the system "azapptoolkit wants to use your confidential information stored in 'azapptoolkit'" dialog; "Always Allow" only lasts until the next update, and "Deny" surfaces as `AuthError::Keyring`, which `restore_session` turns into `Ok(None)` — the operator lands on the sign-in card with no hint that the update caused it, and the subsequent sign-in's `set_generic_password` on the existing item can hit the same ACL again and fail with the misleading `keyring` hint "unlock your keychain". None of this is written down: README/DEVELOPMENT.md cover only the one-time Gatekeeper bypass. Reasoned from Apple's keychain ACL model and the vendored store code; not observed on hardware (no macOS here).
proposal: Short term (docs, S): add to README's macOS section and the Updates section that, because the build is unsigned, macOS asks for keychain access again after every update — choose **Always Allow**; and that a post-update launch that lands on the sign-in card is this, not a revoked session. Medium term: treat Developer-ID signing (stable `identifier + team` designated requirement) as the fix rather than only notarization, and say so in the DEVELOPMENT.md macOS paragraph. Optionally, on macOS only, have `restore_session` log the `keyring` code at warn when the stored version in settings.json differs from CARGO_PKG_VERSION, so support can recognise it.
verifier_notes: Quoted lines are real: README.md:217-219 ('updates in place like the Windows NSIS build'), crates/azapptoolkit-auth/src/token_cache.rs:54-56 registers `apple_native_keyring_store::keychain::Store` (legacy `SecKeychain*` generic-password API, vendored apple-native-keyring-store-1.0.2/src/keychain.rs:72-74), docs/DEVELOPMENT.md:161-164 says unsigned/not notarized, and apps/desktop/src-tauri/src/commands/auth.rs:36-42 maps every restore error (incl. `AuthError::Keyring` -> code `keyring`, dto/lib.rs:168) to `Ok(None)` with an info-level log. The vendored plugin's macOS `install_inner` (tauri-plugin-updater-2.12.0/src/updater.rs:1294-1385) does replace the whole `.app` by rename, so the post-update binary is a new code object. The ACL premise matches Apple's legacy-keychain trusted-application model (unsigned or linker ad-hoc-signed binaries have no stable designated requirement, so the trust entry is bound to the binary hash) — the reviewer correctly flags this as reasoned, not observed on hardware, and the docs wording should hedge accordingly ('macOS may ask for keychain access again after an update'). Nothing in README/DEVELOPMENT/architecture docs mentions Keychain prompts or 'Always Allow' (grep confirms). Small corrections: the misleading hint text is the frontend's own string at web-rs/src/views/sign_in.rs:157-158 ('unlock your keychain/credential manager'), not keyring-crate text; and the optional 'stored version differs' warn-log would need a version field that settings.json does not currently persist. Severity medium is fair for a docs gap that produces a confusing post-update sign-in with a wrong hint; category docs is right.

title: README promises a failed update check 'is logged (see Logs)' but nothing logs it — the launch-check error is discarded on both sides of IPC
rationale: An operator whose fleet never sees updates (proxy blocking github.com, signature mismatch, malformed latest.json) is told by the README to look in the log — and the log is empty. `check_for_update` maps the plugin error straight into a UiError and the launch path pattern-matches `Ok(Some(_))`, dropping `Err(_)` without a trace. This is distinct from F036/F139 (the unread opt-out) and F250 (bug template fields): here the documented diagnostic path does not exist.
proposal: In `updater_err` (or at the two `.map_err(updater_err)?` sites in `check_for_update`/`perform_update`) add `tracing::warn!(error = %e, "update check failed")` / `"update install failed"` — the plugin error Display includes the endpoint status and signature-verification reason and carries no secret. Optionally log `tracing::info!(current, available, "update available")` on `Some(update)`. Effort S; makes README:253 true and gives support a one-line answer to 'why doesn't it update'.

title: audit.rs tests the cache guard exhaustively but nothing tests what feeds `degraded`; score_one's swallowed SP lookup (F023) returns a clean Ok(AuditItem) the guard cannot see
rationale: The predicate test proves 'degraded non-empty blocks the cache' for all 8 combinations, and `a_dead_session_stops_the_audit_but_one_bad_app_does_not` (1621) proves whole-item failures classify correctly — but a failed SP lookup becomes neither: score_one returns `Ok(AuditItem)` with `orgwide == HashSet::new()`, so the run scores the app as scoped, `degraded` stays empty and the guard is fed a lie. `ScoreCtx` (860-880) is `Arc<GraphClient>` + `Arc<Cache>` + resolver, i.e. constructible over wiremock, so this is a missing producer test, not an untestable path.
proposal: Make score_one report coverage: return `(AuditItem, Option<AuditCoverageGap>)` or take `&Mutex<Vec<AuditCoverageGap>>`, pushing `GraphAppRoleAssignments` (or a new `ServicePrincipalLookup`) on the Err arm. Add `a_failed_sp_lookup_degrades_the_run_and_blocks_the_cache`: wiremock `GET /v1.0/servicePrincipals?$filter=appId eq 'app-1'` -> 503 (retry budget exhausted), one app with a Graph mail role granted; assert the gap is reported and `run_is_cacheable(false, false, &degraded) == false`. F029's source-scan pin of the `cache.put` guard is complementary, not a substitute.

title: audit_cancel is shared by the read-only audit, every bulk write and the AAP migration, and the UI can run them concurrently, so any Cancel button stops all of them
rationale: Generation arithmetic: audit claims (current=1, token g=1), then a bulk scope-and-strip/delete claims (current=2, g=2). Pressing Cancel in EITHER the posture strip (cancel_audit) or the BulkProgressRow (cancel_bulk) runs cancel(): cancelled = max(0, 2) = 2, and both 2>=1 and 2>=2 hold, so both runs stop. The reverse start order gives the same result. There is no ordering in which cross-kind collateral cancellation does not happen. Consequences: (1) the operator cancels a read-only scan and a tenant WRITE (bulk delete, scope mailbox/SharePoint access, add owner, disable sign-in, AAP migration) halts mid-selection, reporting 'N app(s) were never attempted' for a Cancel they never pressed on it; (2) the operator cancels a bulk run and the audit result comes back cancelled=true, uncached, and the Security strip shows 'This scan was cancelled early — X of Y principals were scored' (security_view.rs:236-246) — a coverage caveat for a cancel that never targeted the scan. The CancelFlag::cancel doc justifies stopping older generations as 'a run that was going to be superseded anyway', which only holds when all runs on a flag are the same kind; the docstrings' 'never run at once' premise is false given keep-alive views and per-component busy signals, so this is not a documented trade-off. The same overlap also means every mounted BulkActionBar's `use_progress_stream(progress, events::bulk_progress)` (bulk_action_bar.rs:391-392) receives BOTH producers' events, so two concurrent bulk rows show interleaved done/total.
proposal: Give each run kind its own identity. Minimal (S): add `bulk_cancel: CancelFlag` and `migration_cancel: CancelFlag` to AppState, point `cancel_bulk` and all `bulk_*` claims at `bulk_cancel`, the AAP migration at its own flag, and pin the command->flag mapping in repo_invariants/cancel.rs (e.g. a `bulk_*` command body must claim `bulk_cancel`, `run_audit` must claim `audit_cancel`). Robust (M): have `claim()` return the generation to the command, emit it in the first progress event (`run_id` on BulkProgress/AuditProgress), and add a `cancel_run(run_id)` command that does `cancelled.fetch_max(run_id)` only when it is the current generation — then each Cancel button stops exactly its own run and progress listeners can filter by run_id, fixing the interleaved bulk-progress rows too. Update the docstrings at bulk.rs:127, bulk.rs:143-145, audit.rs:14 and caching-and-search.md:350 to state the real rule.
verifier_notes: Evidence is real and the premise is false. bulk.rs:125-134 justifies sharing audit_cancel with 'the two long-running loops never run at once', but nothing enforces that: views are keep-alive (web-rs/src/lib.rs:274, 288), audit_view/mod.rs:239-247 mounts a BulkActionBar (RemoveExpired/Delete) inside the Security view whose `busy` (bulk_action_bar.rs:387, 459-461, 620) is independent of the controller's `scanning` (controller.rs:182-185, which never clears `result`, so the table+bar stay live during a re-scan), bulk_actions_view.rs has only its own `busy`, and there is no session-level long-run gate. CancelFlag::cancel (state.rs:94-97) does `cancelled.fetch_max(current)`, so every older generation on the flag stops; the pinning test `cancelling_also_stops_older_runs_still_in_flight` (state.rs:765-776) and the `cancel()` doc justify that only as 'a displaced run stopping is harmless', which assumes same-kind runs. 12 claim sites share the flag (audit.rs:147, bulk.rs:156/319/418/541/616/674/724/774/842/905, aap_migration.rs:52) plus two cancel commands (audit.rs:478, bulk.rs:133). caching-and-search.md:350 records the sharing ('audit_cancel (audit + bulk)') but not the collateral-cancel trade-off, so this is not a documented decision. The secondary point stands too: every BulkActionBar listens to one `bulk-progress` channel (bulk.rs:12-13, bulk_action_bar.rs:391-392), so two concurrent bulk runs interleave. Severity downgraded from high to medium: the collateral stop is clean (item boundary, unattempted apps named, `incomplete`/`cancelled` flagged, nothing cached or corrupted) and needs two concurrent long runs plus a Cancel; it is a real correctness/UX bug in a write path, not data loss. The Minimal (S) proposal (own `bulk_cancel`/`migration_cancel` flags + pin the command→flag mapping in repo_invariants/cancel.rs) is the right shape under repo conventions; the run_id design is optional.

title: sweep_cancel is shared by the site sweep, Key Vault sweep, mailbox probe and per-app site panel, all of which can run concurrently from always-mounted panels; one panel's Cancel aborts the others
rationale: The premise 'the two never run concurrently from the UI' is contradicted by the Resource Access module doc: the Mailboxes, Sites and Vault access panels are display-toggled, each with an independent busy signal, so an operator can start a site sweep, flip to Vault access and start a KV sweep, then probe a mailbox — three runs on one flag (and the per-app site panel in an app detail adds a fourth entry point). cancel() stamps `current`, so pressing Cancel on the 20-second mailbox probe also aborts a multi-minute site sweep and KV sweep; each then reports 'scan was cancelled early' (sites.rs:127-128, keyvault.rs:137-138) and is deliberately NOT cached, so the operator loses the whole scan and gets a coverage caveat for a Cancel they aimed elsewhere. Additionally two `sweep_site_permissions` runs (Resource Access Sites tab + app panel) can be in flight at once: both subscribe to `site-sweep-progress` (sites.rs:159, app_site_access_panel.rs:52) so their progress interleaves, and the tenant-wide sweep is paid twice because there is no single-flight on the sweep.
proposal: Split into `site_sweep_cancel`, `keyvault_sweep_cancel`, `mailbox_probe_cancel` (or adopt the run_id cancel design from the audit_cancel finding) and give each frontend Cancel its own command; fix the docstrings at permission_tester.rs:443 and docs/architecture/resource-access-and-permission-tester.md:14-15. For the duplicate site sweep, wrap `sweep_site_permissions` in `state.single_flight(&sweep_cache_key(&tenant_id))` with a post-acquire cache re-check so the second caller joins the first's result instead of re-walking every site.
verifier_notes: Evidence verified. permission_tester.rs:441-444 asserts 'the two never run concurrently from the UI'; resource_access/mod.rs:19-20 says all panels stay mounted (display toggle) and each gates only on its own signal (sites.rs:186-189 `scanning`, keyvault.rs:190-193 `scanning`, mailboxes.rs:173 `probing`), so a site sweep, a KV sweep and a mailbox probe can all be in flight at once; app_site_access_panel.rs (do_scan gated on its own `scanning`) is a fourth entry point that calls the same `sweep_site_permissions`. Three commands claim `sweep_cancel` (sharepoint.rs:839, permission_tester.rs:456, keyvault_rbac.rs:96 — the docstring's 'both' is already stale) and four frontend handlers call the one `cancel_resource_sweep` (sites.rs:235, keyvault.rs:239, mailboxes.rs:198, app_site_access_panel.rs:138), which stamps `current` so every older generation stops. resource-access-and-permission-tester.md:12-15 and bindings/keyvault_rbac.rs:3 repeat the premise. Cancelled sweeps are deliberately not cached (sharepoint.rs:989-992; sites.rs:127-128 / keyvault.rs:137-138 render the caveat). The duplicate-sweep point is also correct: `single_flight` is used only in search.rs, gallery.rs and applications/cache.rs, never around the sweep. Severity: medium is fair — read-only, so no tenant harm, but a multi-minute tenant-wide sweep is discarded and a false coverage caveat shown; the false premise appears in three places. Proposal is sound; the single-flight wrap must re-check the cache after acquiring the gate (a cancelled first run caches nothing, so the joiner would legitimately re-run).

title: GraphClient has a single throttle_observer slot, so concurrent fan-outs on one tenant overwrite each other's tracker and ThrottleGuard::drop clears whichever run's observer is installed
rationale: Each FanOutMeter::attach does build its own ConcurrencyThrottle (no shared tracker), and the recovery loop terminates within one 30 s tick after the last Arc drops (Weak upgrade fails -> break), so those two parts are sound. But the observer slot is one `Option` per GraphClient, and the audit, bulk delete/grant/expired-sweep, site sweep and DR backup all run against the same `Arc<GraphClient>` for the tenant. When run B attaches while run A is in flight, A's tracker is silently replaced: A's 429s now halve B's cap and A's own cap never halves again. When either guard drops first, `clear_throttle_observer()` removes the OTHER run's observer for the rest of its life, so a still-running fan-out runs with a fixed cap and no back-off — exactly the 'stale/missing observer' failure the guard exists to prevent, now in the concurrent case the guard's doc never considers. Distinct from F020 (halving window) and F031 (tick ordering).
proposal: Make the slot multi-observer: `RwLock<Vec<Weak<dyn ThrottleObserver>>>`, `set_throttle_observer` pushes, `on_throttle` notifies every live Weak and prunes dead ones, and `ThrottleGuard::drop` removes only its own tracker (`Weak::ptr_eq`). Alternatively keep the single slot but make `clear_throttle_observer` a compare-and-clear (`Arc::ptr_eq` against the guard's own tracker) and log when an attach displaces a live observer. Add a unit test in client/tests/transport.rs that attaches two observers and asserts both see a 429 and that dropping one guard leaves the other attached.
verifier_notes: Verified: `throttle_observer: RwLock<Option<Arc<dyn ThrottleObserver>>>` (client.rs:143) with unconditional overwrite/clear (client.rs:262-268); `ThrottleGuard::drop` clears whatever is installed (throttle.rs:140-144) with no identity check; the transport clones the slot per attempt (transport.rs:557) and `$batch` reads it per throttled round (batch.rs:296), so after a foreign clear every later request sees `None`. All six attach sites (audit.rs:133, bulk.rs:185/326/424, sharepoint.rs:864, backup.rs:88) use the shared per-tenant `Arc<GraphClient>` from `state.graph_for`. Concurrency between these runs is real (see finding 0: keep-alive views, per-component busy flags, audit+bulk in one view; site sweep + audit on different views). The guard doc (throttle.rs:126-131) only considers the sequential/early-return case. The one existing observer test (client/tests/transport.rs:~290) attaches a single observer. Not handled elsewhere. Severity honest at medium: the consequence is loss of adaptive back-off (fixed cap, no halving) for the surviving run, while the per-request `with_retries` still honours Retry-After, so it degrades rather than fails — but it defeats the exact contract the guard exists for, and AGENTS.md lists the adaptive throttle as an invariant. Either proposal works; the compare-and-clear (`Arc::ptr_eq` against the guard's own tracker, plus a warn when an attach displaces a live observer) is the smaller change; multi-observer `Vec<Weak<_>>` is more correct since Graph pressure on one tenant is genuinely shared. A two-observer transport test is the right pin.

title: Startup panics with zero diagnostics if the log file cannot be created: install_tracing `.expect()`s the appender before any subscriber or panic hook exists
rationale: `create_dir_all`'s error is ignored, then `build()` is unwrapped. On a read-only or unwritable app-data dir (locked-down %APPDATA% redirection, a sandboxed/kiosk profile, HOME unset so the fallback is the install directory) the very first thing the process does is panic — before `install_panic_hook` and before any `tracing` subscriber — so a double-clicked GUI app 'just doesn't open', the advertised log directory holds nothing, and stderr is invisible. The panic hook's own doc comment (lib.rs:374-378) explains exactly why an unlogged crash is unacceptable; this path defeats it.
proposal: Install the panic hook first (it only needs `tracing` macros, which are no-ops until a subscriber exists — or buffer: install a stderr-only subscriber first). Make the file appender optional: `match builder.build(&log_dir) { Ok(a) => Some(non_blocking(a)), Err(e) => { eprintln!(...); None } }`, register the file layer via `.with(file_layer_option)` (tracing-subscriber supports `Option<Layer>`), then after init `tracing::warn!(log_dir = %log_dir.display(), error = %e, "file logging disabled")`. Consider surfacing the same fact in the config screen / About so the operator learns the log is not being written. Effort S.

title: Restored dock mounts every parked detail pane hidden at launch, each firing its full Graph detail fetch before Home paints
evidence:
open_items_workspace.rs:138: `<For each=move || session.open_items.get() key=|it| it.id let:item>` and :238 `style:display=move || if shown() { "flex" } else { "none" }`
state/tenant.rs:38: `self.restore_open_items();` (inside `set_active_tenant`, i.e. at sign-in/restore)
state/open_items.rs:217-218: `/// `shown_items` is deliberately left empty — the dock comes back, the\n/// overlay does not.` and :240 `self.open_items.set(restored);`
application_detail_pane.rs:39-51: `let detail = LocalResource::new(move || { ... applications::get_application_detail(&t.tenant_id, &id).await })` (fires on mount, not on show)
applications/mod.rs:252-282: wave 1 `try_join(get_application, list_owners)`, wave 2 `get_service_principal_by_app_id`, wave 3 `try_join(list_app_role_assignments, list_oauth2_grants)`, then `resolve_required_resource_access`
rationale: `restore_open_items` repopulates `open_items` during `set_active_tenant`, the keyed `<For>` mounts a window for every item, and each pane's `detail` LocalResource runs on mount regardless of `shown`. So an operator who parked 8 items (F370: unclamped) pays 8 x (4 Graph waves + permission resolution) — roughly 40 Graph calls plus 8 IPC payloads — the instant the shell appears, none of them visible (the overlay is deliberately closed), all competing with Home's five tenant-wide scans on the same per-tenant Graph throttle and the same tokio runtime. frontend-workspace.md:124-126 documents mounting ALL windows so that chip switches don't refetch, which is an interactive-time argument; it says nothing about restore, and the restore path has no design note. The chip labels come from `open_items` titles, so the dock needs no pane to render.
proposal: Gate each restored window on first show: in `open_item_window`, wrap the pane body in the existing `keep_alive`-style visited latch seeded from `shown_items` (mount when `shown()` first becomes true, then keep alive), or give `OpenItem` a `restored: bool` that defers the body until focused. Items opened interactively keep today's eager behaviour. Expected effect: launch Graph traffic drops by up to ~40 calls and 8 detail payloads on a full dock; chips still restore instantly. Add a GUI test in the open_items_dock shard asserting that a restored, un-shown item records no `get_application_detail` invoke.
verifier_notes: All cited evidence checks out: open_items_workspace.rs:131 mounts the overlay whenever open_items is non-empty (independent of shown_items), :138 keyed <For> mounts a window per item, :238 hides by style:display; tenant.rs:38 calls restore_open_items() inside set_active_tenant (which runs at sign-in/session restore — CHANGELOG line 32 confirms the session is restored at launch and line 86 confirms the dock is 'parked per tenant across restarts'); open_items.rs:217-218 + :240 restore open_items with shown_items deliberately empty. views/application_detail_pane.rs:39-51 creates the detail LocalResource unconditionally on mount (enterprise_application_detail_pane/mod.rs:104 likewise), and get_application_detail (mod.rs:252-282) is the 4-wave fan-out described. frontend-workspace.md:124-126 documents mount-all for chip-switch reuse only; nothing documents restore-time eager fetching, and no GUI test covers the restore path (tests/gui/open_items_dock.rs has no restore/parked case, though its mock_details at :47-50 mocks get_application_detail so an invoke-count assertion is straightforward). The proposed building block exists: util.rs:24 keep_alive is a Show-when-visited latch. MAX_OPEN_ITEMS = 8 (open_items.rs:19) and restore does not clamp, so the worst case is 8 hidden panes. Only caveat (not a refutation): the eager fetch does warm the backend app_detail| cache so a later chip click is instant — a trade-off worth a design note, but the operator lands on Home per the restore comment, so paying ~40 Graph calls plus 8 detail payloads before any pane is visible, concurrently with Home's tenant-wide scans, is the wrong default. Severity medium is fair for a full dock; with 1-2 parked items the cost is minor.

title: Webview panics and IPC rejections are never persisted: console_error_panic_hook writes only to the webview console and there is no frontend→backend log command
rationale: F425 documents that any non-UiError IPC rejection panics the whole WASM app. When that (or any other frontend panic — an `expect` in a view, a Leptos runtime error) happens in a release build, the operator sees a frozen or blank window; the panic message exists only in a devtools console that release builds cannot open, so a bug report can contain nothing but 'it went blank'. The backend log, the one artifact support asks for, is silent because nothing bridges the two worlds.
proposal: Add `#[tauri::command] fn log_frontend(level: String, message: String)` (three-step pattern: command, `generate_handler!`, `bindings/diagnostics.rs` stub) that re-emits at `tracing::{warn,error}!(target: "webview", %message)` with a length cap. In `run()`, replace `set_once()` with `std::panic::set_hook(Box::new(|info| { console_error_panic_hook::hook(info); let msg = info.to_string(); leptos::task::spawn_local(async move { let _ = invoke_result::<()>("log_frontend", ...).await; }); }))`. Also call it from `Session::report_command_error_for` for the plain-toast branch so IPC failures the operator saw are in the log with their `code`. Register a no-op fixture in `demo::register_fixtures` (enforced by `demo_fixture_coverage.rs`) and gate the invoke on `not(feature = "demo")` if simpler. Effect: WASM panics and surfaced UiErrors land in the same daily file as backend events.

title: `unauthorized` (client 401, including the CAE "re-auth needed" path) renders as bare "unauthorized (401)" with no action; the three ui_hints tell the operator to sign out, contradicting the in-place recovery design
rationale: `unauthorized` is deliberately excluded from `REAUTH_FATAL_CODES` (reauth.rs:64-81) so a fan-out keeps going — that rationale is about halting loops, not about what the operator sees. On screen a Graph 401 (revoked token, CAE challenge the silent re-mint could not satisfy) is the text `unauthorized (401)` in a toast or `unauthorized (401) [unauthorized] Retry` in DetailLoadError, while the remedy the transport itself names ("surfaces to the caller to re-auth") lives one click away as the top-bar "Refresh token" control (shell.rs:492) whose handler already falls back to `reauthenticate` on a dead session. Meanwhile the Exchange/KV/ARM hints say "Sign out and back in", which AGENTS.md ("A dead session forces re-auth in place… never sign the user out") and the shell comment ("still no sign-out, so the cached lists + audit run survive") explicitly reject, and `premium_feature_err` says "Your session expired. Sign in again" (graph_err.rs:88-91) with no control to do so. F353/F427 cover the *dead-session* codes not reaching the sink; this is the 401 class, which reaches the sink and is still a dead end.
proposal: 1) Extract shell.rs's refresh-token handler into `Session::spawn_refresh_token()` (silent `refresh_session` → on `is_reauth_fatal` fall back to `reauthenticate`). 2) In `report_command_error_for`, add a branch before the plain toast: `if e.code == "unauthorized" { push_toast(Error, "Your access token was rejected — refresh it and retry.", Some("Refresh token"), Some(spawn_refresh_token)) }`. Do NOT add the code to `REAUTH_FATAL_CODES`. 3) Reword the three `Unauthorized` ui_hints and `premium_feature_err`'s Unauthorized arm to "use Refresh token (next to Sign out), then retry" — the Exchange `Forbidden { had_diagnostics: false }` hint already uses exactly that phrasing. 4) Add a GUI test next to tests/gui/reauth.rs asserting an `unauthorized` mock produces a toast with a "Refresh token" action.
verifier_notes: All cited evidence is real. No `"unauthorized"` branch exists anywhere in apps/desktop/web-rs/src, so a Graph 401 (transport.rs:610-611 plain 401; 663-664 and 677-683 CAE re-mint failure) falls through `report_command_error_for` to a plain toast of `unauthorized (401)`. The three `ui_hint`s say 'Sign out and back in' (crates/azapptoolkit-arm/src/error.rs:32-35, keyvault/src/error.rs:35-37, exchange/src/error.rs:124-128) and graph_err.rs:88-91 says 'Sign in again', contradicting AGENTS.md ('never sign the user out') and the in-place design already implemented by the shell Refresh-token handler (views/shell.rs:116-146: `refresh_session` → on `is_reauth_fatal` → `reauthenticate`). The Exchange `Forbidden{had_diagnostics:false}` hint already uses the correct 'use "Refresh token" (next to Sign out), then retry' wording (exchange/error.rs:116-122), so the reword is consistent with existing copy. `unauthorized` is correctly excluded from `REAUTH_FATAL_CODES` (core/reauth.rs:32,64-81) and the proposal preserves that. tests/gui/reauth.rs covers only `refresh_missing`/`not_signed_in`, so a new GUI test is the right pin. Severity is at the low end of medium: access tokens refresh ~60 s before expiry so a 401 is an anomaly (revocation/CAE), and the remedy is one click away; the hint reword (S effort) is independently worthwhile even if the toast action is deferred.

evidence:

rationale: The Graph client's own comment states the hazard precisely — a host that accepts no connection burns the whole total timeout once per attempt — but the fix was applied to Graph only. For a SYN-blackholed `management.azure.com`, `*.vault.azure.net`, `outlook.office365.com` or `api.loganalytics.io` (typical of an egress allow-list that admitted graph.microsoft.com only), each attempt runs to the 60 s ceiling (Linux/macOS; Windows' TCP stack gives up at ~21 s), and every transport retries network failures three times: 4×60 s + (1+2+4) s ≈ 247 s for ARM/KV/Exchange and 4×120 s + 7 s ≈ 487 s for a Log Analytics usage query. Reads have no `CancelToken`, so the operator sees a skeleton / "Loading…" / disabled button for four to eight minutes and then, per finding 2, `network: error sending request for url (…)` with no cause. The SSO metadata probe's `unwrap_or_default()` additionally falls back to a `reqwest::Client::default()` with no timeout at all if the builder ever fails.

The SSO metadata probe's `.build().unwrap_or_default()` (apps/desktop/src-tauri/src/commands/sso/mod.rs:1282-1285) does fall back to `reqwest::Client::default()`, which has no timeout. title: Retry/throttle log lines carry no endpoint, status or reason — a 429 storm and a 5xx outage look identical, and inner $batch 429 re-batches are silent
evidence:
http_retry.rs:207-212 (the only log line on the retry path):
  tracing::warn!(
      attempt = budget.attempt(),
      label,
      retry_after_secs = ?retry_after_secs,
      "transient failure; retrying"
  );
crates/azapptoolkit-graph/src/client/transport.rs:552: `let outcome = with_retries("graph", retry_class, |_| {` — constant label, attempt number discarded, nothing logged inside the closure.
crates/azapptoolkit-graph/src/client/batch.rs:283-300 (inner-429 re-batch loop): the only side effect is `obs.on_throttle(max_retry_after)` and `budget.wait(max_retry_after).await;` — no tracing call.
rationale: The task's headline failure mode — a 429 storm during a 10k-app audit — produces N identical `transient failure; retrying label="graph" attempt=1 retry_after_secs=Some(…)` lines plus `throttle: throttled, reducing in-flight cap`. `RetryReason` (Throttled vs Transient) and the HTTP status are not logged, so a Graph 503 incident and a tenant-quota 429 are indistinguishable in the file; the endpoint family (`/servicePrincipals`, `/$batch`, `/sites/{id}/permissions`) is unknown, so the engineer cannot tell which fan-out is being throttled. When the budget is exhausted nothing is logged at all — the error becomes a toast. The `$batch` path, 'the throttle-happiest endpoint in the API' per its own comment, logs no inner retries.
proposal: (1) Log `reason = ?reason` and the retried error's `ui_code()`/status in `with_retries` (E: Display is available; add a `status: Option<u16>` to `Attempt::Retry` or log `%err`). (2) Pass a label that names the request: `format!("graph {method} {path}")` where `path` is the URL with query stripped (`url::Url::path()`) — no `$filter` values, hence no PII; ARM/KV can do the same. (3) In `batch_chunk`, `tracing::info!(throttled = throttled.len(), pending = urls.len(), attempt = budget.attempt(), ?max_retry_after, "$batch: re-batching throttled sub-requests")` and a `warn!` when the budget is spent. (4) When `!budget.may_retry()` log `warn!(label, attempts, "retry budget exhausted")` before returning `Err(err)`. Effort S; all inside `http_retry`/transport, covered by existing paused-clock tests.

title: No failure (or mutation) logging at the command boundary: 15 write-command files contain zero tracing calls and the UiError conversion/frontend sink never log, so a failed or destructive operation leaves no trace in the log
rationale: The operator reports 'Remove password failed' or 'the tool disabled sign-in on the wrong app'. The log has nothing: the Graph transport logs no terminal failure, the `From` conversion is a pure map, the toast is ephemeral. Even successful destructive writes (bulk delete, disable sign-in, AAP migration, DR restore) leave no local record of which object was touched when — only Entra's server-side audit log knows, which the support engineer may not have access to. Backend-wide there is exactly one `error!` (the panic hook) and 65 `warn!`s, none on the common command failure path.
proposal: One boundary hook instead of ~50 edits: (1) give the `backend`-feature `ui_error_from!` arms (and `From<AuthError>`) a `tracing::warn!(code = %ui.code, retryable = ui.retryable, source = %err, "command error")` — add `tracing` as an optional dep of `azapptoolkit-dto` under `backend`; body text is already what flows to the UI (F290 covers capping it). (2) Feed the same hook into a small `AppState` ring buffer of the last N UiErrors (code, message, UTC timestamp) for the diagnostics bundle. (3) For mutations, add an `info!` line in the shared write cores that are already single-sourced (`remediate_*` cores, `run_bulk_seq`, `invalidate_app_*` call sites are natural choke points) naming command, tenant id and object id. Pin (1) with a unit test that a `GraphError::Forbidden` conversion emits a warn (tracing-test or a capturing subscriber). Effect: every failed command and every destructive write has a timestamped log line.

title: Network errors drop the cause: reqwest 0.13 `Display` prints only "error sending request for url (…)", so every `network`/`network_error` message hides DNS/timeout/TLS/proxy
rationale: Since reqwest 0.12 the `Display` impl no longer appends `source()`, so `err.to_string()` yields `error sending request for url (https://graph.microsoft.com/v1.0/applications?$top=999)` for a DNS failure, a connect timeout, a TLS interception failure and a proxy 407 alike. The desktop shows this verbatim via DetailLoadError / toast (`network: error sending request for url (…)`), and the sign-in card shows `error [network]: http: error sending request for url (https://login.microsoftonline.com/…/oauth2/v2.0/token)` with the generic hint. The one piece of information an operator behind a corporate proxy needs ("connection timed out" vs "dns error" vs "invalid peer certificate") is available on `reqwest::Error` (`is_timeout()`, `is_connect()`, `source()` chain) and is discarded at all six construction sites. README/F247 asks for proxy/TLS guidance; without the cause on screen, that guidance cannot be matched to a symptom.
proposal: Add one helper in `azapptoolkit-core` (gated off wasm32, next to `http_retry`): `pub fn describe_transport_error(e: &reqwest::Error) -> String` that emits a class prefix (`timed out` / `could not connect` / `request failed`) and walks `std::error::Error::source()` to append the root cause ("dns error: failed to lookup address…", "connection refused", "invalid peer certificate…"). Use it at the six `Network(err.to_string())` sites (Graph transport ×2, ARM, KV, Exchange ×2) and in `AuthError::Http`'s Display (`#[error("http: {}", describe(.0))]` or a manual impl). Expect the operator-facing string to become e.g. `network: could not connect (connection timed out) — https://graph.microsoft.com/…`. Add a unit test with a reqwest error built from a refused localhost port asserting the cause appears.
verifier_notes: Premise verified against the vendored source: reqwest 0.13.5 (Cargo.lock:3915-3916) `impl Display for Error` (registry reqwest-0.13.5/src/error.rs:257-304) writes only the kind text (`error sending request`) plus ` for url (…)`; `source()` is exposed separately and never appended. Every construction site discards it: 12 `Network(e.to_string())` sites in total (graph transport.rs:32,47,143,157,571,582; arm transport.rs:60,69; keyvault client.rs:196,205; exchange transport.rs:188,197 — six are send failures, six are body-read failures), plus `AuthError::Http` displays as `http: {0}` (crates/azapptoolkit-auth/src/error.rs:47-48). Only Exchange logs the error with `?err` (Debug, which does include `source`), so the cause reaches the log there but never the UI. Two corrections: the README has no proxy/TLS guidance at all (grep for proxy/firewall/corporate/egress finds nothing; 'F247' is a sibling finding, not repo content), so drop that justification; and `azapptoolkit-core` does not depend on `reqwest` (crates/azapptoolkit-core/Cargo.toml:22-26 lists parking_lot/async-trait/tokio/url only), so the proposed `core::describe_transport_error` adds a new (non-wasm-gated) dependency to core — acceptable but should be called out given AGENTS.md's 'dependencies are a cost', or the helper can live in a crate that already has reqwest and be re-used.

title: Graph/ARM/Key Vault transports send no client-request-id and never capture request-id/Date — Microsoft-support correlation is impossible for every non-Exchange failure
rationale: Microsoft Learn ('How to debug Microsoft Graph API calls', 'Best practices for working with Microsoft Graph § Reliability and support') says: generate a unique GUID per request, send it as `client-request-id`, log it, and always log the response `request-id` and `Date` — 'they're required when you report issues ... to Microsoft Support. Without these headers, diagnosing the issue is difficult.' Today a Graph 403 (`forbidden (403): {body}`), a 404, a post-budget 5xx or a 429 surfaces with status+body only; there is no identifier a support engineer can hand to Microsoft, and no log line at all is written for the terminal failure in the transport. The repo's own DEVELOPMENT.md policy ('log the ui_code/request id') is met only by the Exchange client.
proposal: In `send_core_url_with` (and `scoped_get`/`scoped_send_core`, ARM `send_with_retry`, KV `send_core_url`): (a) mint a v4 GUID per logical request (move `commands::guid::new_v4_guid` into `azapptoolkit-core` so the crates can use it; `rand` is already a dependency) and set `client-request-id`; (b) on any non-success capture `request-id`/`client-request-id`/`Date` (ARM: `x-ms-request-id`, `x-ms-correlation-request-id`; KV: `x-ms-request-id`; batch: the same keys from each sub-response `headers` map) and append them to the error detail the way Exchange's `compose_error_detail` does (`… (request-id: …, client-request-id: …)`) so the UiError message and any toast carry them; (c) emit one `tracing::warn!(method, path_without_query, status, request_id, client_request_id, "graph request failed")` at the terminal-failure site (Attempt::Done(Err(..)) paths and budget exhaustion). Pin with a wiremock test in `tests/transport.rs` asserting the request header is present and the ids appear in the error. Effect: every failure in the log and the UI is correlatable by Microsoft support; the 429/5xx question 'which endpoint' becomes answerable.

title: Bug template tells reporters to read the version 'From Help → About', but the Help submenu is empty and exists only on macOS; the version actually lives in the account menu
evidence:

title: sp_index_tests is a weaker copy of its app_name_index twin: the untyped-get test asserts only `.is_none()` (which the twin's own comment says cannot tell a miss from an eviction) and the invalidate_app_lists case is missing
rationale: Both indexes ride the same `get_typed`/poison path, so the SP index is exposed to exactly the eviction regression the app_name twin now guards with `Arc::ptr_eq` after the untyped read (417-424). The module doc promises the two are mirrors; they diverged when the app_name half was fixed. `invalidate_app_lists` does drop `sp_index_key` today (cache.rs:113), so the missing test is a ratchet, not a live bug.
proposal: Copy the two missing assertions into `sp_index_tests`: after the untyped `get`, `sp_index_hit(..).expect(..)` and `Arc::ptr_eq(&stored, &hit)`; add `invalidate_app_lists_drops_the_index` (t1 dropped, t2 kept). Optionally turn both modules into one macro-instantiated table so they cannot drift again.

title: The security audit — the app's flagship long run — writes no start/finish summary line (duration, totals, coverage gaps, cancelled), unlike the site sweep
rationale: 'The audit took 40 minutes / stopped at 60% / shows fewer findings than yesterday' are the questions a support engineer gets; the log cannot answer any of them — a fully successful run of 10k apps leaves zero lines, a cancelled run leaves zero lines, and the `degraded` coverage gaps (which the UI correctly refuses to cache) are never recorded. The site sweep already demonstrates the one-line pattern.
proposal: At `run_audit` entry `tracing::info!(%tenant_id, "audit started")`; capture `Instant::now()`; at the end `tracing::info!(total, scored = items.len(), unscored, degraded = ?degraded, cancelled, elapsed_secs = start.elapsed().as_secs(), "audit complete")`. Same two lines for `backup_tenant`, `restore_tenant` and the `bulk_*` commands via `run_bulk_seq` (count, failed, cancelled). Effort S.

title: Offline at launch is folded into `Ok(None)`: the sign-in card steers an operator with a still-valid refresh token into an interactive sign-in that cannot succeed, with no offline cue or restore retry
rationale: The documented rationale ("the card is the recovery, and it already says what to do") holds for the cases the comment lists — nothing stored, a revoked token, a locked keyring — where the correct next step really is to sign in. It does not hold for the case the comment omits: the token endpoint is unreachable (laptop off-network, captive portal, proxy down). The refresh token is still valid (only `InvalidGrant` purges it), yet the operator is told to "Sign in to your tenant"; clicking opens a browser that cannot load login.microsoftonline.com, the loopback listener then waits up to 300 s (F113) and returns `loopback`, whose hint is the generic fallback. Nothing on screen ever says "you appear to be offline", and there is no way to retry the silent restore once connectivity returns short of restarting the app. The backend already computes the code (`UiError::from(err).code`) and throws it away.
proposal: Keep the command signature. In `restore_session`, compute `let ui = UiError::from(err)` (already done at auth.rs:40) and return `Err(ui)` only when `ui.code == "network"`; every other failure keeps `Ok(None)` and the documented rationale. In `Root` (web-rs/src/lib.rs), capture that `Err` into a signal and render `SignInScreen` with a `Callout tone="warn"` reusing `sign_in.rs::recovery_hint("network", …)` wording plus a 'Retry' button that re-invokes `bindings::auth::restore_session()` (not `sign_in`). Extend the auth.rs doc comment to name the offline case as the one exception. Add a GUI test mocking `restore_session` with a `network` UiError asserting the callout renders and `sign_in` is not called. No demo fixture work is required.
verifier_notes: Code path verified: `restore_session` folds every error into `Ok(None)` after computing and logging the code (apps/desktop/src-tauri/src/commands/auth.rs:37-44); the frontend ignores `Err` too (apps/desktop/web-rs/src/lib.rs:167-174); the service's restore performs a real refresh-token POST (`access_token_for_scopes`, auth/service/mod.rs:614-617) and only `InvalidGrant` purges the refresh token (mod.rs:529-540), so offline → `AuthError::Http` → token retained → sign-in card. The loopback wait is 300 s (mod.rs:274). However this IS a documented deliberate decision — the command's doc comment (auth.rs:20-31) states `Ok(None)` is the answer for 'every way this can come up empty' and argues a launch-time error toast is noise. The finding's real contribution is that the enumerated cases omit 'token endpoint unreachable', where 'sign in' is not the right next step. Proposal is over-scoped: the demo build skips the restore entirely (`#[cfg(not(feature = "demo"))]` at lib.rs:161-162; no `restore_session` fixture exists in demo/ or tests), so no fixture update is needed; and a new `RestoreOutcome` enum is a wire-shape change touching the binding when the existing `Result<Option<_>, UiError>` already has an `Err` arm nobody uses. Severity low: narrow window (offline at launch), the refresh token survives so relaunching online just works, and the sign-in flow's `network`/`loopback` hints eventually say to check the network.

title: sign_out prunes only graph_clients and exchange_clients; kv_clients, arm_clients and la_clients survive sign-out
rationale: Not a credential leak: every client holds a ScopedTokenAdapter that asks the singleton auth service per request (token_adapter.rs:70-80), so a stale client fails with `not_signed_in` after sign-out. But the asymmetry is unexplained, the kv map is keyed per (tenant, vault) and only grows across a long session with several tenants/vaults, and a long-running fan-out that outlives sign-out keeps its `Arc<GraphClient>` and stops only when its next `bearer()` fails (dispatch::SessionDead) — sign_out cancels none of the three flags, so a bulk write continues until that failure and a run in its final local phase can still `cache.put` a `{tenant}|…` entry (e.g. audit.rs:441-446) after `invalidate_tenant` swept the tenant. The window is small, but it is the same-tenant/different-operator case the sign_out comment says it exists to prevent.
proposal: In sign_out remove the tenant's entries from all five client maps (`kv_clients.lock().retain(|(t, _), _| t != &tenant.tenant_id)`, `arm_clients`/`la_clients` `.remove(&tenant.tenant_id)`) and add a repo_invariants test that every `Mutex<HashMap<…, Arc<…Client>>>` field on AppState is referenced in `sign_out`. Do NOT cancel `audit_cancel`/`sweep_cancel`/`dr_cancel` there unless the flags become tenant-keyed — they are process-global and would abort another signed-in tenant's run; rely on `SessionDead` (the next `bearer()` fails with not_signed_in) as today. If the post-invalidate cache-put window matters, guard the final `cache.put` in run_audit/sweep on the session still being alive rather than cancelling globally.
verifier_notes: Asymmetry confirmed: auth.rs:52-53 removes only `graph_clients` and `exchange_clients`; `kv_clients` (keyed per (tenant, vault)), `arm_clients` and `la_clients` (state.rs:207-214) have no references anywhere outside state.rs, so nothing ever removes them. Not a credential leak — `ScopedTokenAdapter::bearer` re-asks the auth singleton per request (token_adapter.rs:69-82), so a stale client fails with not_signed_in. The post-invalidate `cache.put` window (audit.rs:441-446 after `invalidate_tenant`) is real but tiny and requires sign-out to land between the last Graph read and the put. The 'cancel all three flags in sign_out' half of the proposal has a flaw the finding misses: the cancel flags are process-global, not tenant-keyed, while `sign_out` takes one `TenantContext` and AppState is explicitly multi-tenant ('Each signed-in tenant gets its own GraphClient'); `CancelFlag::cancel` stamps the current generation, so signing out tenant A would abort a run on tenant B. Pruning all five maps and adding the repo_invariants check is a clean improvement; the flag cancel should be dropped or made conditional.

title: Untyped errors force prose oracles: conditional_access, credentials and cert tests can only distinguish failure causes by substring-matching operator messages because the code collapses them into one code or a bare String
rationale: In each case two distinct causes (licence vs consent; end-before-start vs over-cap; bad CN vs bad validity) share one code or a `Result<_, String>`, so the test's only discriminator is copy text — a wording edit breaks the suite while a swapped classification would not necessarily fail it, and the frontend cannot branch on the cause either. The rest of the slice's prose asserts (readiness role names, tester `detail` sentences) sit beside a typed `Verdict`/`verdict` assertion and are acceptable as secondary checks.
proposal: Split `ca_unavailable` into `ca_license_required` / `ca_consent_required` (or add a typed `reason` field); give `resolve_password_window` and `generate_self_signed` a small error enum with a stable `code()` mapped into `UiError`; rewrite the four asserts to compare codes/variants and keep at most one prose assertion per test on the exact user-facing sentence.

title: Cold launch runs three concurrent /applications paginations (pairing rows, credential roll-up, app-name index) whose projections nest, and the pairing scan seeds neither of the other two caches
evidence:
credentials.rs:63-72: `.list_applications_all(
    AppListQuery::default()
        .with_top(PAGE_SIZE)
        .with_select(vec!["id", "appId", "displayName", "passwordCredentials", "keyCredentials"]),
    Some(MAX_APPS),
)`
applications/mod.rs:53-63: `fn list_row_select() -> Vec<&'static str> { vec!["id", "appId", "displayName", "signInAudience", "publisherDomain", "createdDateTime", "passwordCredentials", "keyCredentials"] }` and :176 `client.list_applications_all(query, Some(APPS_MAX)).await?`
applications/cache.rs:334: `.list_application_index_named(Some(super::APPS_MAX))` (select `id,appId,displayName`)
home_dashboard.rs:29/44/69: `let apps = LocalResource::new(...)` / `let enterprise = ...` / `let creds = ...` all fire on mount
docs/architecture/caching-and-search.md:35: `There are exactly **two** cached tenant-wide directory enumerations, and no surface may run its own:`
rationale: Home's five resources fire together on a cold tenant, so `list_applications_with_pairing` (list_row_select), `list_enterprise_applications` -> `app_name_index_cached` (id,appId,displayName) and `list_credential_expirations` (5 fields) each page the whole `/applications` collection concurrently: 3 x ceil(N/999) serial round trips (18 for 5,000 apps), two of them selecting `keyCredentials`, which applications.rs itself notes is under a 150-req/min/tenant throttle. `list_row_select` is a strict superset of both other projections, and `apps_pairing_key` and `credential_expirations_key` are invalidated by exactly the same two tiers (`invalidate_app_lists` at cache.rs:234-263 and `invalidate_app_credentials` at :277-292 both bust both keys), so the roll-up can be produced from the same scan with no freshness change. The pairing command already seeds the SP index from its own scan (mod.rs:181-193) but never seeds `app_name_index` from the `Vec<Application>` it holds, so the Enterprise card's join immediately re-enumerates the apps it just fetched. This also contradicts the caching doc's own invariant. F007 covers the SP-side duplicate; this is the /applications side.
proposal: In list_applications_with_pairing (mod.rs ~157-222): take generation_for watches for app_name_index_key and credential_expirations_key before the scan (alongside the existing apps_pairing watch); after the scan, store (a) a lean projection of the apps (id/app_id/display_name only, ..Default::default()) via app_name_index_store_if_current, and (b) summarize_credentials rows (factor the row build out of credentials.rs into a shared fn) via put_index_if_current under credential_expirations_key. In list_credential_expirations and app_name_index_cached, before their own scan, acquire-and-release state.single_flight(&apps_pairing_key(tenant)) so a pairing scan in flight lands first, then re-check their own cache and fall back to their existing scan on a miss (the pairing rows cannot rebuild the credential roll-up). Expected effect: on a cold tenant the launch costs one /applications pagination instead of three; warm/partial cases are unchanged. Drop the allowlist pin; the existing watch-capture-order invariant already covers the new stores.
verifier_notes: Evidence is real: credentials.rs:62-75 scans /applications with a 5-field $select; applications/mod.rs:53-64 list_row_select is a strict superset of that and of the app_name_index projection (cache.rs:334 list_application_index_named = id,appId,displayName); home_dashboard.rs:29/44/69 create the apps/enterprise/creds LocalResources on mount, and enterprise -> list_enterprise_applications -> indexes_cached -> app_name_index_cached (enterprise_application.rs:93, cache.rs:315-337) is a third cold /applications pagination. Both keys are busted by the same two tiers (cache.rs:108+126 in invalidate_app_lists, :149+157 in invalidate_app_credentials; no other invalidator of apps_pairing_key), and mod.rs:181-193 seeds the SP index but never app_name_index. The 150/min keyCredentials throttle note is real (graph client/applications.rs:214). Corrections: (1) the 'contradicts the caching doc' claim is a stretch — caching-and-search.md:35 is about the two lean *indexes*, and credentials.rs:9-16 explicitly documents this as a second scan of the same collection mitigated by caching under the same freshness contract, i.e. a known, partly-deliberate choice rather than an unnoticed violation; (2) the wall-clock benefit is overstated — the three scans already run concurrently, so the credential card does not land 'after its own scan'; the real win is 3x fewer /applications requests (18->6 at 5k apps, 33->11 at 10k), two of them carrying keyCredentials, and less contention with the SP scans and any restored dock fetches — bandwidth/CPU/throttle headroom on very large tenants, not user-visible latency on typical ones, hence severity low; (3) the proposal to have list_credential_expirations 'call the pairing core instead of scanning' cannot work alone: ApplicationListRowDto rows are lean scalars (caching-and-search.md 'Filtering happens in the frontend, on lean rows'), so when apps_pairing is warm but credential_expirations is cold (LRU-evictable per finding 3, or stored at different times) the pairing core returns a hit and yields no credential rows — the credential command must keep its own scan as a fallback; (4) seeding app_name_index from the pairing scan must project down to id/appId/displayName first, or the 'lean' pinned index holds every app's credential arrays in memory for the 60-min TTL; (5) a repo_invariants allowlist of list_applications_all( call sites cuts against the repo's 'derive, don't list' style (fanout.rs:18 already uses that string as a TENANT_WIDE_READ marker).

title: Credential-expiry roll-up is stored unpinned although cache.rs names it as a pinned tenant-wide index
evidence:
credentials.rs:97: `state.cache.put(CacheKind::Lists, cache_key, &rows);`
core/cache.rs:711-720 (doc of `put_index`): `/// Like [`Self::put`], but marks the entry **pinned**: exempt from LRU eviction ... Use only for tenant-wide *index* entries that cost a full directory scan to rebuild and that several surfaces read — the service-principal index, the app-registration pairing rows, the credential-expiry roll-up. These share a bucket with thousands of cheap per-app entries, so without the pin a single mail-heavy audit run evicts them`
For contrast, enterprise_application.rs:115 and managed_identity.rs:88 use `state.cache.put_index_if_current(watch, &rows);`
rationale: F006 already records that this store is unguarded against the store-after-invalidate race; what is new is that it is also the only tenant-wide roll-up written with plain `put`, so it is LRU-evictable by the per-app `app_detail|`/`mail_scopes|` churn that shares the `Lists` bucket — exactly the scenario the `put_index` doc describes — and the doc claims it is pinned when it is not. The effect is a silent full `/applications` rescan for the Home credential card and the Credential Expiry tab after a detail-heavy audit or browsing session, within the 60-minute TTL.
proposal: Take `let watch = state.cache.generation_for(CacheKind::Lists, &cache_key);` before the scan and replace the `put` with `state.cache.put_index_if_current(watch, &rows);` (one change fixes both F006 and the pin); add the key to the repo_invariants pin that covers the other `put_index_if_current` list stores. If finding 1 is adopted the store moves into the pairing core and inherits its watch.
verifier_notes: credentials.rs:97 is a plain state.cache.put(CacheKind::Lists, ...), while core/cache.rs:711-720 (put_index doc) explicitly lists 'the credential-expiry roll-up' among the pinned tenant-wide indexes — so the doc claims a pin the code does not have. The eviction mechanism is real: the Lists bucket is capped at MAX_PER_OBJECT_CACHE_SIZE = 10,000 (cache.rs:601-603, constants.rs:70) and shares that cap with per-app app_detail| writes (mod.rs:292) and per-app mail_scopes|audit|{app}| writes the audit makes (exchange/mail_scopes.rs:249-254, plus declared|/held| variants), so a mail-heavy audit or heavy browsing on a large tenant can LRU-evict the unpinned roll-up within its 60-min TTL and force a silent full /applications rescan for the Home card and the Credential Expiry tab — exactly the scenario the put_index doc describes. The sibling list stores (enterprise_application.rs:115, managed_identity.rs:88, mod.rs:220) all use put_index_if_current, so this is the one outlier. Two small corrections to the proposal: the repo_invariants pin does not keep a per-key list for the _if_current forms (cache.rs:130-145 skips them; the watch-capture-order test covers them), so no PINNABLE_KEYS/allowlist edit is needed — just take generation_for(CacheKind::Lists, &cache_key) before the .await at credentials.rs:62 and store via put_index_if_current(watch, &rows); and the 'found >= 5' floor in pinned_cache_writes_stay_on_the_tenant_wide_indexes simply counts one more. Severity low is honest (a redundant rescan, no wrong data). If finding 0 is adopted the store moves into the pairing core with its own watch.

title: AAP migration claims a cancel token 'so the operator can stop it' but no UI surface exposes a Cancel; the only things that stop it are the audit and bulk Cancel buttons
rationale: The claim satisfies the repo_invariants rule for tenant-wide writers, but functionally the operator still cannot stop a migration from the surface that started it, so the comment's stated goal is unmet. Worse, because it rides audit_cancel, the migration IS stopped by unrelated Cancel presses (a running audit scan's Cancel, or any BulkActionBar Cancel), returning `incomplete: true` with the app in `unattempted` — see the audit_cancel finding. Since both UI callers are per-app (one batch), the check at aap_migration.rs:95 fires at most once, so today the token mostly serves the dead-session latch.
proposal: Either give the migration its own flag plus a Cancel button in the Exchange scoping section's busy state and in the MigrateLegacyScope dialog (S), or, if per-app runs are the only supported shape, drop the 'operator could not stop a whole-tenant migration' comment and document that cancellation here exists only for the SessionDead break. Do the former if `app_id: None` is meant to become a UI feature.
verifier_notes: Verified. aap_migration.rs:36-42 says the operator 'could not stop a whole-tenant migration once started' and claims `audit_cancel` (line 52); the only two frontend callers (exchange_scoping_section.rs:332-338, dialogs/migrate_legacy_scope.rs:69-74) both pass `Some(&app_id)` and neither file contains 'cancel'; the only frontend cancel callers are cancel_audit, cancel_bulk, cancel_resource_sweep and cancel_dr. With `app_id: Some`, `group_policies_for_migration` yields one batch, so the `is_cancelled() || is_dead()` check in the `while let` loop (aap_migration.rs:~95) runs once, before the only write — it can honour a Cancel pressed during the preceding reads (via an unrelated audit/bulk Cancel button) and nothing else. One correction to the rationale: the repo_invariants detector (`dispatch_capped(` / `run_bulk_seq(` / `report.cancelled = true`) does not match this command (it uses a local `cancelled = true` and `incomplete: cancelled`), so the claim here is not actually what satisfies the invariant — removing it would not fail CI, which makes the 'fix the comment vs wire a Cancel' decision purely a product one. The binding accepts `app_id: Option<&str>`, so a whole-tenant run is reachable from code but not from any UI. Proposal is reasonable; if per-app stays the only shape, also consider extending the invariant detector to cover this loop shape.

title: managed_identity.rs tests stop at ARM scope-string classification; the per-subscription flatten that duplicates management-group assignments (F072) has no test and no seam
rationale: The nearest test proves the 'Management group' label is produced for MG-scoped ids, i.e. the code expects such rows, but the fan-out/flatten that receives the same MG row once per subscription is inline in the `State` command and untested; a dedupe-by-assignment-id regression would ship silently.
proposal: Extract `flatten_assignments(per_sub: Vec<(String, Option<Vec<RoleAssignment>>)>) -> Vec<(String, RoleAssignment)>` that dedupes on `RoleAssignment.id` (keeping the first subscription label, or labelling MG rows by scope) and test: two subscriptions each returning assignment `ra-1` at `/providers/Microsoft.Management/managementGroups/mg` plus one sub-scoped `ra-2` -> exactly two rows.

title: Startup banner records only version and log_dir — OS/arch, cloud, configured tenant id and build profile are missing, so the first thing support needs is not in the log
evidence:
lib.rs:368-372:
  tracing::info!(
      version = env!("CARGO_PKG_VERSION"),
      log_dir = %log_dir.display(),
      "azapptoolkit starting"
  );
state.rs:248-256 logs the tenant/client id only when they are UNSET (`"AZAPPTOOLKIT_TENANT_ID is not set; sign-in will fail until configured"`); nothing logs the resolved value or its source (env / settings.json / baked). bug_report.yml:36-43 asks the operator to type the OS by hand.
rationale: A log tail sent by an operator should self-describe: which OS/arch (Windows chunked keyring vs macOS), which cloud (sovereign endpoints), which tenant the session was for, whether it is a debug build, and where the ids came from (env override vs settings.json — the README's three-way resolution is a classic support question). Today all of that must be asked back.
proposal: Extend the banner: `os = std::env::consts::OS, arch = std::env::consts::ARCH, debug = cfg!(debug_assertions)`, and after `AppState::new` log `tracing::info!(cloud = ?env, tenant_id = %tenant_id, tenant_id_source = "env|settings|baked", client_id_source = ..., "resolved auth config")` (tenant id is already logged by the auth crate at service/mod.rs:534, so no new exposure). Effort S.

title: Daily debug-level logs (14 files) are written to Roaming AppData on Windows instead of LOCALAPPDATA
rationale: `%APPDATA%` is the Roaming hive; Windows convention (and Tauri's own `PathResolver::app_log_dir`, which resolves to `%LOCALAPPDATA%\<identifier>\logs`) puts logs and caches under Local because Roaming is synchronised with roaming user profiles / FSLogix / UE-V at logon and logoff. The MSI is explicitly marketed for SCCM/Intune/GPO estates — the population most likely to roam profiles — and this app writes at `debug` level for its own crates, two weeks of it, so the profile carries megabytes of request logs (with tenant/object GUIDs) between machines and slows logon. settings.json belongs in Roaming (it is per-user config); the logs do not. The comment at lib.rs:333-337 documents the path but gives no roaming rationale, so this is a convention slip rather than a decision.
proposal: Introduce `log_directory()` per platform: Windows `%LOCALAPPDATA%\azapptoolkit\logs` (fallback to `%APPDATA%` only if LOCALAPPDATA is unset), macOS `~/Library/Logs/azapptoolkit` (the platform convention), Linux `$XDG_STATE_HOME`/`~/.local/state/azapptoolkit/logs` or keep `.local/share` but honour `$XDG_DATA_HOME`. Keep settings.json where it is. Update README Logs + the lib.rs comment, and add a one-line CHANGELOG note since the documented log location changes for operators. Consider a one-time best-effort move of existing log files so support instructions stay valid.
verifier_notes: Evidence is accurate: apps/desktop/src-tauri/src/lib.rs:395-399 resolves `config_directory()` from `%APPDATA%` (Roaming) on Windows and :391-393 puts logs under it; the default filter at :330-331 is `azapptoolkit=debug,desktop=debug` with 14 daily files (:354); README.md:426 documents `%APPDATA%\azapptoolkit\logs`. Tauri's own convention is verified in vendored tauri-2.11.6/src/path/desktop.rs:278-290: `app_log_dir` = `dirs::data_local_dir()/<identifier>/logs` (LOCALAPPDATA) on Windows/Linux and `~/Library/Logs/<identifier>` on macOS. The lib.rs comment (:333-337) states the paths with no roaming rationale, and no doc, CHANGELOG or .claude/rules entry records a decision to roam logs, so this is a convention slip rather than a deliberate choice. Not pinned by any repo_invariants test. Severity downgraded from medium to low: the harm (profile bloat / slower logon / GUID-bearing logs following the user) is real but modest and confined to roaming-profile / FSLogix estates, and it is an enhancement, not a defect. The proposal is reasonable and self-contained (keep settings.json in Roaming, move only logs, update README Logs + the lib.rs comment, CHANGELOG note because the documented support path changes); a best-effort one-time move is optional.

title: AppState cancel-flag field docs describe the retired AtomicBool reset model and name a command that does not exist
rationale: CancelInner's own doc (state.rs:42-56) explains that `reset()` was removed precisely because it was a destructive write, yet the three field docs 40 lines below still say 'Reset to `false` at the top of every run' / 'Reset at the top of every sweep'. `audit_cancel` is also flipped by `cancel_bulk`, and `sweep_cancel` covers the KV sweep and mailbox probe and is flipped by `cancel_resource_sweep`, none of which the docs mention. F030 covers the stale reset narrative in run_bulk_seq, the deep-dive and cancel.rs, but not these field docs, which are the first thing a reader of AppState sees.
proposal: Rewrite the three field docs: name every command that claims each flag and every command that cancels it, drop the 'Reset…' sentences, and reference `CancelFlag::claim`. If the flags are split per the other findings, do it in the same edit.
