title: A network failure during the lazy token refresh surfaces as non-retryable `token_error` instead of `network_error`: `token_adapter::token_error` flattens `AuthError::Http` like every other non-fatal variant
rationale: Extends F110 (which covers `consent_required`). The same outage produces two different classifications depending on where it strikes: during the Graph call it is `network_error` (retryable: true, "network: …"); during the lazy refresh that precedes the call (`provider.bearer()` at transport.rs:498, ~every hour) it is `token_error` (retryable: false) with message `token: http: error sending request for url (https://login.microsoftonline.com/<tenant>/oauth2/v2.0/token)`. The auth-plane spelling `network` is hinted only on the sign-in card, so mid-session it never receives a hint either. Operators and any future `network_error`-specific UI treatment (finding 3) will miss the refresh-time half of network failures.
proposal: In `token_adapter::token_error`, add `AuthError::Http(_) => "network_error"` only (leave `TokenExchange` as `token_error` unless `azapptoolkit-auth` later splits a genuine 5xx variant). In `core::reauth`, add a small `TRANSIENT_PASSTHROUGH: &[&str] = &["network_error"]` (or a `passthrough_any` fn) and have `http_error_enum!`'s `Token(t)` arm and `ExchangeError::ui_code` pass it through alongside the fatal codes so `is_retryable` sees one `network_error` class regardless of hop. Extend the dto `reauth_agreement_tests` (or a new adapter test) to pin that `AuthError::Http` maps to a retryable, non-reauth-fatal code on both planes, noting the intentional `network` (auth plane) vs `network_error` (client plane) spelling.
verifier_notes: Premise verified: `token_adapter::token_error` maps `AuthError::Http(_)` (and everything else non-fatal) to `"token_error"` (apps/desktop/src-tauri/src/token_adapter.rs:22-27); `passthrough_code` only passes `REAUTH_FATAL_CODES` (crates/azapptoolkit-core/src/reauth.rs:50-52), so `ui_code()` yields `token_error`; `is_retryable_code` excludes it (core/http_retry.rs:25-27). A network failure during the lazy refresh therefore surfaces as non-retryable `token_error` with message `token: http: error sending request for url (…)`, whereas the same outage during the Graph call is retryable `network_error`. The adapter's own doc ('The codes must match `UiError`'s — `From<AuthError> for UiError` is the source of truth', token_adapter.rs:19-20) is already violated since dto maps `Http` → `("network", true)` (dto/lib.rs:169). Not documented as deliberate. The `TokenExchange → "server_error"` half of the proposal is unsafe and should be dropped: `classify_token_error` (crates/azapptoolkit-auth/src/service/wire.rs:44-62) returns `TokenExchange` for every AAD error that is not invalid_grant/consent — including permanent 4xx like `invalid_client`/`unauthorized_client` — and `post_token` also returns it for any non-JSON non-success (`HTTP {status}` from a proxy block page, mod.rs:198); classing those as retryable `server_error` would make configuration errors retry and mislabel them. Severity low agreed: refresh-time failures are a small fraction of outages and the message is still recognisably a network error.

title: trunk build --release ships unminified CSS and JS: Trunk's `minify` defaults to `never` and nothing enables it
evidence:
Trunk.toml:1-6: `[build]\ntarget = "index.html"\ndist = "dist"\n# Optimization is selected by the caller's `--release` flag ... so there is no `release` default to set here.` (no `minify` key)
justfile:51-52: `web-build-release:\n    trunk build --release --locked`
index.html:19-22: `data-wasm-opt="z"` ... `<link data-trunk rel="css" href="styles.css" />`
styles.css is 120,706 bytes (`wc -c`).
Upstream trunk `src/config/types/minify.rs`: `pub enum Minify { /// Never minify #[default] Never, /// Minify for release builds OnRelease, /// Minify for all builds Always }` and `src/config/models/build.rs`: `/// Control minification. #[serde(default)] pub minify: Minify,`
rationale: The index.html comment shows the team already tuned the wasm side (`wasm-opt=z`, and Cargo.toml's `opt-level = "z"`, `lto`, `strip`) for startup, but Trunk applies `minify` separately and its default is `Never`, so the release bundle carries the 120 KB stylesheet and the wasm-bindgen JS glue verbatim (comments, whitespace, long identifiers). Every webview start parses them; a typical minify pass removes 30-40% of the CSS and more of the glue. The cost is modest because assets load from the local asset protocol, but the fix is one config line and has no effect on the GUI tests (they build via `cargo test`, not Trunk) or the dev loop (`on_release` leaves `trunk serve` untouched).
proposal: Add `minify = "on_release"` under `[build]` in apps/desktop/web-rs/Trunk.toml (or `--minify` in `web-build-release` and `web-build-pages`), rebuild once and eyeball the Pages demo for any CSS the minifier changes semantically (custom properties and `@media` blocks are safe). Pin the Trunk version CI installs (`tool: just,trunk` is unpinned in ci.yml/release.yml/pages.yml) so the minifier behaviour is reproducible.
verifier_notes: Verified: apps/desktop/web-rs/Trunk.toml has no minify key (its comment covers only the --release/optimization default); upstream trunk-rs/trunk main Trunk.toml documents `minify = "never" # can be one of: never, on_release, always` as the default; the justfile web-build-release and web-build-pages recipes pass --release --locked with no --minify; grep finds no minify anywhere in the repo; index.html tunes wasm-opt=z and Cargo.toml [profile.release] sets opt-level z / lto / codegen-units 1 / strip, so the wasm side is tuned while CSS (styles.css = 120,706 bytes) and the wasm-bindgen JS glue ship verbatim; GUI tests build via cargo test/wasm-pack, not Trunk, so they are unaffected, and on_release leaves trunk serve alone. One nuance on the secondary 'pin Trunk' step: taiki-e/install-action is pinned by SHA (v2.87.17) in ci.yml:152, pages.yml:44 and release.yml:131, and that action bundles its tool manifests, so the trunk version CI installs is already implicitly fixed by the action pin (it moves only when the action is bumped); an explicit `trunk@x.y.z` would make it visible but is not strictly needed. Dev boxes (scripts/setup.sh:66 `cargo install trunk --locked`) are the genuinely unpinned path. Severity low is honest — assets load from the local asset protocol, so this is parse/startup and bundle-size hygiene, not a user-visible regression.

title: `UiError.retryable` drives a Retry action on only one surface; the toast-only paths (`run_toast_err`, direct `report_command_error`) never offer one despite the DTO doc promising a retry button
rationale: The DTO contract says `retryable` advises a retry button, every client computes it via `is_retryable_code` (throttled/server_error/network_error), and the toast primitive supports a sticky Retry action — yet the only consumer is the admin-consent button in permissions_tab. `report_command_error_for` always passes `None`, and the pinning test (state/mod.rs:722-731) asserts a `network` error with `retryable: true` gets no action. errors.rs:70-74 explains the sink cannot replay because it receives only the `UiError`, but `CommandState::run_toast_err` *does* hold `op`; it just types it `FnOnce` so it cannot be re-invoked. Net effect: a 429/5xx/network failure on any of the ~24 `run`/`run_toast_err` call sites and the ~56 inline `error.set(Some(e.message))` sites is a 10-second auto-dismissing red toast (errors without an action are not sticky, toast.rs:129) with no way back except finding and re-clicking the control — the exact "dead end" the module docs say the sink exists to prevent.
proposal: Scope the change to the toast-only paths rather than every runner: add an `Option<ToastAction>` parameter to `report_command_error_for` (keep `report_command_error` passing `None`), and in `run_toast_err` only, accept `op` as `Rc<dyn Fn(String) -> Fut>` (or `impl Fn + Clone`) and pass a replay closure when `e.retryable`; leave `run`/`run_with` signatures untouched since their inline `error` sits beside the re-clickable control. Flip the state/mod.rs:722-731 pin only for the `run_toast_err` path. Alternatively, amend the `UiError` doc (dto/lib.rs:42-43) to say `retryable` is advisory and consumed where a replay closure exists, and keep the wire field for `DetailLoadError`/permissions_tab.
verifier_notes: The mechanics are real: `.retryable` is read at exactly one site (apps/desktop/web-rs/src/views/tabs/permissions_tab.rs:121); `report_command_error_for` always passes `None` (state/errors.rs:160); errors without an action auto-dismiss (components/toast.rs:129); `run_with` takes `op: impl FnOnce` (hooks/use_command.rs:48) so it cannot replay; and state/mod.rs:722-731 pins `retryable: true` → no action. But the 'dead end' framing is overstated: (1) `DetailLoadError` always renders a Retry button for every load failure regardless of the flag (detail_load_error.rs:36-43), so load surfaces are covered; (2) `CommandState::run` (28 call sites) writes the inline `error` signal next to the control that triggered it, so the operator re-clicks in place — only `run_toast_err` (16 sites) and the 15 direct `report_command_error*` callers are toast-only; (3) by the time `throttled`/`server_error`/`network_error` reaches the UI, `with_retries` has already spent MAX_RETRIES=3 attempts honoring Retry-After (core/http_retry.rs), so an immediate manual retry has limited value; (4) errors.rs:70-74 documents why the sink cannot replay. The '112 of 113 surfaces' figure counts inline-error sites that do not need a toast action. Not a documented decision to drop the flag, so the doc/behaviour mismatch is genuine but small.

title: Backup and restore share dr_cancel and are gated by independent signals in the DR view, so the backup's Cancel also stops an in-flight restore (reported as a partial restore)
rationale: The DR view renders the Back up and Restore controls side by side; 'Back up this tenant' is disabled only while `busy` (dr.rs:237) and 'Restore into this tenant…' only while `restoring` (dr.rs:361-366), so an operator can start a backup and, while it walks a large tenant, load a file and start a restore. Both claim dr_cancel (gen 1 and gen 2); cancel_dr stamps current=2, so the backup's Cancel button stops the restore between passes. The restore report then reads '(cancelled before completing — partial)' (dr.rs:494) for a run whose Cancel button was never pressed, leaving shells created without permissions/owners/secrets. The backup-and-restore.md rationale only argues dr_cancel vs audit_cancel; it never considers backup vs restore overlap.
proposal: Frontend (S): make the two flows mutually exclusive on the page — disable/hide 'Restore into this tenant…' and 'Load backup file…' while `busy`, and disable 'Back up this tenant' while `restoring`. Optionally backend (S): add `restore_cancel: CancelFlag` + `cancel_restore` command so only the restore's own Cancel can stop the write; update restore.rs:359 and backup-and-restore.md to say backup and restore never overlap (or have separate flags). Drop the 'bare shells' claim — passes 2-5 already finish wiring created apps after a cancel.
verifier_notes: The cross-cancel is real: dr.rs:55 gates backup on `busy` only, dr.rs:150-155 `do_restore` never reads `busy`, the Restore controls are hidden only while `restoring` (dr.rs:361-366) and the Back-up button disabled only while `busy` (dr.rs:237); both cancel handlers call `cancel_dr` (dr.rs:96-98, 180-182); both commands claim the same `dr_cancel` (backup.rs:78, restore.rs:193) and restore.rs:359 acknowledges the sharing without considering overlap; backup-and-restore.md:126-128/173 only argue dr_cancel vs audit_cancel. But the stated consequence is wrong: restore.rs passes 2-5 each check `is_cancelled()` per item and, per the design comment (restore.rs:184-186) and backup-and-restore.md:173-175, a cancel 'stops creating new apps but still finishes wiring the created ones — never bare shells'; the report says '(cancelled before completing — partial)' (dr.rs:494) and names the apps. So the outcome is a clean, reported partial restore, not stranded shells. Severity lowered to low: the scenario (starting a restore into a tenant while backing it up, then pressing the backup's Cancel) is unusual, and the stop is clean; the fix is still worth making because it is trivial and removes a DR footgun.

title: `target = "azapptoolkit::graph"` / `"azapptoolkit::cache"` are recorded as a field named `target`, not as the event target, while both layers hide the real target with `with_target(false)`
evidence:
service_principals.rs:188-192:
  tracing::debug!(
      target = "azapptoolkit::graph",
      first_page = page.items.len(),
      "service-principal index first page"

Same form at service_principals.rs:209,216,257; commands/applications/mod.rs:143,151; enterprise_application.rs:74,77; managed_identity.rs:57,60; permissions.rs:55,58 (`tracing::debug!(target = "azapptoolkit::cache", kind = "Lists", key = %key, "hit")`).
tracing-0.1 macros.rs:21,55,663: the target override is spelled `target: $target:expr`; `$($k:ident).+ = $($fields:tt)*` is the field arm.
lib.rs:359-365:
  .with(fmt::layer().with_target(false).compact())

title: DEVELOPMENT.md says the NSIS installer 'asks once about per-user vs per-machine'; the config uses Tauri's default currentUser mode, so nothing asks
rationale: Tauri's NSIS `installMode` defaults to `currentUser`; only `both` shows the per-user/per-machine chooser. `bundle.windows` sets nothing for NSIS, so the installer silently installs per-user — which is also what the README and the release-body row ("per-user, auto-updates") say and what the updater's passive `/P /UPDATE` relaunch relies on (a per-machine NSIS install would need elevation the passive updater does not request). DEVELOPMENT.md therefore contradicts both the shipped behaviour and the sibling docs; a contributor who 'fixes' the config to `both` to match the doc would break silent updates for anyone who picked per-machine.
proposal: Rewrite the sentence to "installs per-user with no prompt and no admin rights (Tauri's default `currentUser` NSIS mode — keep it that way: the passive updater relaunch depends on it)". One-line docs edit; optionally pin with a repo_invariants check that `bundle.windows.nsis.installMode` is absent or `currentUser`.
verifier_notes: Confirmed docs contradiction. docs/DEVELOPMENT.md:179-181 says the NSIS installer 'asks once about per-user vs per-machine'; apps/desktop/src-tauri/tauri.conf.json:38-42 sets no `bundle.windows.nsis.installMode`, and updater-build.json only sets `createUpdaterArtifacts`. Vendored tauri-utils-2.9.3/src/config.rs:819-841 shows `NSISInstallerMode` defaults to `CurrentUser` and only `Both` offers the chooser (and `Both` 'will require Administrator access even if the user wants to install it for the current user only' — so the doc's implied no-admin tester flow is impossible under the chooser anyway). README.md:189-190, release.yml:295 and DEVELOPMENT.md:137 all say per-user/no admin, so :180 is the odd one out. One overstatement in the rationale: switching to `both` would not outright 'break' passive updates — the NSIS `/P /UPDATE` relaunch would trigger a UAC prompt rather than fail silently — but the doc fix is still correct and the warning against flipping the mode is worth keeping in softer form. Severity low, one-line docs edit; the optional repo_invariants pin is cheap but not required.

title: Shipped frontend bundle size (dist .wasm/.js/.css) is never measured or recorded — only the debug GUI-test shards are gated
evidence:
justfile:146-150: `web-itest-size:
    ...
    CEILING_MB=52
    DEPS=target/wasm32-unknown-unknown/debug/deps` (measures `gui_*.wasm` test shards only)
justfile:51-52: `web-build-release:
    trunk build --release --locked` (no size output)
docs/architecture/release-updater-demo.md and docs/DEVELOPMENT.md: grep for `bundle`/`wasm`/`size`/`KB`/`MB` finds only the WebView2 runtime (`~127 MB`) and CHANGELOG-baking notes — no figure for the shipped `.wasm`/`.js`/`.css`.
rationale: The repo has invested heavily in wasm size for the test shards (a 52 MB ceiling, opt-level notes, a strip rationale) because size failures there are opaque, but the artifact that matters to operators — the release wasm the webview instantiates at every launch — has no recorded baseline, so a dependency bump or a new view that doubles it (Leptos view trees are known to bloat) lands unnoticed until someone complains about startup. There is no number to compare a `just web-build-release` against, and the release workflow uploads `bundle/` without reporting what is inside.
proposal: Add a `web-size` recipe (Unix/CI like web-itest-size) that prints raw and gzip byte sizes of apps/desktop/web-rs/dist/*.wasm, *.js and *.css and requires an existing dist (no rebuild). Call it from release.yml on one leg (e.g. Linux, after the build step) and from pages.yml after web-build-pages, appending to $GITHUB_STEP_SUMMARY; do not add it to verify-full (it would break the recipe's CI-parity contract and add a minutes-long release build). Record today's release-build numbers in docs/architecture/release-updater-demo.md next to the bundle/crypto notes, and optionally have web-size warn (not fail) past ~1.5x that wasm baseline via an env-overridable threshold.
verifier_notes: Premise verified: justfile web-itest-size measures only target/wasm32-unknown-unknown/debug/deps/gui_*.wasm against a 52 MB ceiling; web-build-release prints nothing; ci.yml:177 is the only size step and it is that shard gate; release.yml and pages.yml have no size reporting; docs/DEVELOPMENT.md and docs/architecture/release-updater-demo.md mention only the ~127 MB WebView2 runtime and CHANGELOG baking — no figure for the shipped .wasm/.js/.css exists anywhere. So there is no baseline and a regression would land silently. The proposal needs one correction: wiring web-size into verify-full would force a release Trunk build (lto + opt-level z + wasm-opt z, minutes) that verify-full does not run today (_verify-core ends with the debug web-build) and that CI does not run as a gate either — the justfile's own comment (justfile ~323-329) insists verify-full mirror CI exactly, so adding a local-only step there violates that contract. Also, the Pages bundle includes the demo feature and its fixtures, so it is not the shipped artifact; the true number comes from the release.yml legs (dist exists after cargo tauri build's beforeBuildCommand) and is identical across the 3-OS matrix, so report it once. Severity low is honest.
